# Review-thread fetch, acme/widget#82 (N=1)

**Aliases.** `ROOT=/work/widget`, `W=/work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry`, `H=aaaa…aaaa` (40× `a`, home headRefOid), `B=bbbb…bbbb` (40× `b`, origin/main). Provisioning and the base merge are already done. This narration covers only the thread fetch, which runs before gather.

**Owner and cwd.** The query text belongs to `reference/pr-head.md` › *Fetch unresolved review threads*, and I cite it rather than copy it. It runs once per admitted PR, N=1 included. I run every `gh` command from the unchanged session cwd (`/private/var/folders/…/eval-skill-ak9WeJ`). Owner, repo and number are passed explicitly, so cwd does not matter.

**Command legend**

| ID | Command |
|---|---|
| Q1 | `gh api graphql --paginate -f query='<owner reviewThreads query>' -F o=acme -F r=widget -F n=82` |
| Q2 | `gh api graphql --paginate -f query='<owner thread-comments query>' -F id=<T1 id>` |

Q1 uses the reviewThreads cursor. Q2 uses a separate per-thread comment cursor.

---

## A. Successful fetch

**1. Run Q1.** `--paginate` returns three reviewThreads pages, and I merge them into one node list.

| Page | Nodes |
|---|---|
| 1 | T1, unresolved, `src/retry.ts`, line 12. Comments: totalCount=102, hasNextPage=true. |
| 2 | T2, unresolved, outdated, `src/old.ts`, line=null, originalLine=7. Also TX, resolved, `src/gone.ts`, line 2. |
| 3 | T3, unresolved, `README.md`, line=null, originalLine=null. |

**2. Filter `isResolved == false`.** This keeps T1, T2 and T3 and drops TX.

**3. Paginate T1's comments with Q2.**
- Trigger: T1's comment connection reports `hasNextPage: true` and `totalCount 102 > 100`.
- Q2 starts at T1's first comment page, using its own cursor, not the reviewThreads cursor. It continues until `hasNextPage` is false.
  - Page 1 holds 100 comments: the first comment plus replies 1–99.
  - Page 2 holds replies 100 and 101.
- I replace T1's initial comments with this complete connection, so no comments are duplicated. That gives 102 comments in order.
- T2 and T3 need no follow-up, because their comment pages are complete.

**4. Render.** All comments are kept in order. Each one carries url `https://github.com/acme/widget/pull/82#discussion_r1`, author `reviewer` and createdAt `2026-01-01T00:00:00Z`, as supplied. Location follows the owner's rule: `<path>:<line>`, else `<path>:<originalLine> (outdated)`, else `<path>`.

| Thread | Location | Comments (in order) | Effective request |
|---|---|---|---|
| T1 | `src/retry.ts:12` | #1 "Rewrite the retry engine"; replies 1–100 "Rewrite still requested"; reply 101 "Correction: keep the engine; cap retries in two lines." | **Changed.** Keep the existing retry engine and cap retries in a two-line change. The rewrite request is withdrawn by reply 101. |
| T2 | `src/old.ts:7 (outdated)` | #1 "Keep this guard"; reply "Yes, retain it" | Retain the guard. The reply confirms the request. |
| T3 | `README.md` | #1 "Document the cap" | Document the retry cap in README. |

I read the first request and every reply, because a reply can change the request. That is what happened in T1. Reading only the first page or only the first comment would have carried the obsolete rewrite request into gather.

**Record carried to gather (PR #82):**
```
Threads (#82): 3 unresolved
- T1 src/retry.ts:12 — keep engine; cap retries in two lines (corrected by reply 101 of 101; supersedes "Rewrite the retry engine")
- T2 src/old.ts:7 (outdated) — keep this guard (confirmed by reply)
- T3 README.md — document the cap
```

Gather and spec then proceed with these threads and with `MEMBER_HEADS = []`.

---

## B. Failed fetch (independent case)

**Run Q1.** `gh` fails with `API unavailable`.

**Stop**, before gather and before the spec. This rule applies to this N=1 run just as it would to a multi-PR list:

```
threads for #82 not fetched (API unavailable)
```

- No spec is drafted, no Rework record is written, and no `Threads:` line is recorded.
- Nothing is pushed, and no reviewer is dispatched.
- The worktree `W` stays as provisioned, on `fix/retry` at `H`.
- Post-verification fetch-failure reporting is owned by finishing and does not apply here.

---

## C. Successful empty set (independent case)

**Run Q1.** It succeeds. After merging pages and filtering `isResolved == false`, no threads remain, so there is no comment pagination.

**Record:**
```
Threads: none
```

Gather continues with no thread obligations for #82.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.text:
I’m using the using-git-worktrees skill to set up an isolated workspace. This narration covers **only review-thread fetching**, after the stipulated successful provisioning.

### Command and query legend

- `ROOT=/work/widget`
- `W=/work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry`
- PR: `acme/widget#82`; number `82`.
- Every command below has **cwd `$W`**. No cwd-changing command runs.
- `Q_THREADS` denotes the exact review-thread query owned by **`reference/pr-head.md` → “Fetch unresolved review threads.”**
- `Q_COMMENTS` denotes that section’s exact thread-ID comment-pagination query. These aliases stand for the full query arguments; the queries are not copied here.
- `--paginate` follows each connection’s `endCursor` until `hasNextPage=false`. Thread and comment cursors remain separate.

These are three **independent runs**, not successive mutations.

### 1. Successful paginated fetch

| Order | Exact command, using query aliases | Observation / resolved values |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `gh api graphql --paginate -f query="$Q_THREADS" -F o=acme -F r=widget -F n=82` | Fetches all three review-thread pages. Merge their nodes. Unresolved IDs: `T1`, `T2`, `T3`; exclude resolved `TX`. `T1.comments.totalCount=102`, with initial `hasNextPage=true`. |
| 2 | `gh api graphql --paginate -f query="$Q_COMMENTS" -F id=T1` | Starts T1’s comments from their first page, using its own comment cursor. Fetches through the last page, including reply 101. Replace—not append to—T1’s initial comments with this complete connection. |

Cursor strings are response-supplied values consumed by `--paginate`; the case provides no literal cursor strings.

**Metadata legend:** Every comment below retains this supplied metadata:

```text
url: https://github.com/acme/widget/pull/82#discussion_r1
author: reviewer
createdAt: 2026-01-01T00:00:00Z
```

Ranges below represent separate comments in their original order, each carrying that metadata; they are not deduplicated.

| Thread and rendered location | Complete ordered comments | Resulting repair request |
|---|---|---|
| `T1` — `src/retry.ts:12` | **1:** “Rewrite the retry engine” → **2–101 (replies 1–100):** “Rewrite still requested” → **102 (reply 101):** “Correction: keep the engine; cap retries in two lines.” | **Keep the existing engine; cap retries in two lines.** The final correction supersedes the earlier rewrite request. |
| `T2` — `src/old.ts:7 (outdated)` | **1:** “Keep this guard” → **2:** “Yes, retain it” | Retain the guard. Preserve the outdated-location designation. |
| `T3` — `README.md` | **1:** “Document the cap” | Document the retry cap. |

With the documented `first:100` comment query, T1’s first comment page contains its opening comment and replies 1–99; the later page contains replies 100–101, including the correction.

**Record:** `Threads: 3 unresolved` — carry all **105 comments**, with metadata and order preserved, into gather. `TX` at `src/gone.ts:2` is resolved and is not carried as an unresolved thread. Fetching succeeds; no thread-fetch stop applies.

### 2. Independent failed fetch

| Order | Exact command; cwd `$W` | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `gh api graphql --paginate -f query="$Q_THREADS" -F o=acme -F r=widget -F n=82` | Fails: `API unavailable` |

**Stop immediately:**

```text
threads for #82 not fetched (API unavailable)
```

This gate applies to this **N=1** run. Do not enter gather, draft a spec, or continue with a substitute thread record.

### 3. Independent successful empty fetch

| Order | Exact command; cwd `$W` | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `gh api graphql --paginate -f query="$Q_THREADS" -F o=acme -F r=widget -F n=82` | Successful complete fetch; unresolved set is empty. |

Render:

```text
Threads: none
```

No comment follow-up query is needed. No thread-fetch stop applies.

Two small drifts in After are worth watching though: it no longer names the `node(id:)` mechanism for the T1 comment follow-up (only `-F id=<T1 id>` against an 'owner thread-comments query'), which a stricter reading of the threads fact could count against it, and it now says every `gh` command runs from the session temp cwd (`/private/var/folders/…/eval-skill-ak9WeJ`) rather than ROOT, contradicting the Before's 'ROOT is the process cwd, which never changes'. To keep Before's margins while delivering the Change, keep the thread-fetch section wording that explicitly says the follow-up uses `node(id:)` with the thread's own comment cursor, and keep the cwd/ROOT definition intact—the rebase/replay changes should only touch provisioning and member-replay text, not the shared cwd or query-owner legend used by the thread-fetch narration.

Both outputs name the pr-head.md 'Fetch unresolved review threads' section as the query/pagination owner (After is slightly more explicit, citing reference/pr-head.md by filename), merge all three thread pages, exclude resolved TX, fetch T1's comments by thread id with a separate comment cursor through the last page while replacing rather than appending the initial connection, render replies 1-100 before reply 101, and derive the two-line cap repair from the correction. Neither fact moved. Locations (src/retry.ts:12, src/old.ts:7 (outdated), README.md), the exact stop line before gather and spec with no draft/record continuation, and Threads: none for the empty set are all present. Neither listed fact moved: After preserves the query-owner delegation, independent pagination, complete ordered comments and metadata, corrected two-line repair, locations, failure stop, and empty rendering. For clarity, explicitly describe the owner’s comments query as node(id: T1) with its own comment cursor. After does change command execution from W to ROOT; to deliver the requested selected-worktree targeting while keeping process cwd unchanged, retain cwd=ROOT and explicitly execute each fetch in W, for example with `(cd "$W" && gh api ...)`. Keep the existing thread rendering and failure/empty behavior unchanged.
